IDA and Ghidra agree exactly on 178 bytes, 69 instructions and 8 basic blocks; angr agrees on the same extent. The divergence is real and is now explained and fixed: the reference narrows the config-register number to a byte (movzx eax, bl, 0f b6 c3) before sending getRegister:device:function:bus:data:, and ours pushed the full 32-bit int. Mechanism confirmed by experiment: the receiver at IOPCIDirectDevice.m:59 was an untyped id, and this GCC applies no declared method signature to an id receiver, which is why declaring the parameters unsigned char in PCIKernBus.h changed nothing when it was tested (out/i386/mach_kernel, SHA-256 DA6E06AE910CFDC48BA33B8648CBCFB74EE7DCBC904BBA180B9CD86DA06F02AD). The fix is commit 53f1fc3a, which types getThePCIBus()'s return and the six receiver locals in IOPCIDirectDevice.m as PCIKernBus *. In the resulting kernel (out/i386/mach_kernel, SHA-256 A82940452938737FB8514C334434CEAF70B4DC39179A4047B4153D9B589325C1, built 2026-07-26 11:47) this method contains 0f b6 c3 and matches the reference on the checked byte patterns. Held at unexamined deliberately: the entry awaits the measured reference-versus-rebuilt comparison and is not advanced on inspection again, which is what went wrong in the fix pass. Edited directly in ledger.json because the binrecon ledger CLI is forward-only and cannot express the earlier reset (ledger.py:269). See divergences.md Finding 2.

IDA reports 176 bytes, 67 instructions and 5 basic blocks; Ghidra reports no function here; it is the first function of its object file and is preceded by three zero pad bytes; angr agrees on the same extent. The divergence is real and is now explained and fixed: the reference tests the BOOL result of [thePCIBus isPCIPresent] with cmp al, 1 (3c 01) and ours tested the whole register with cmp eax, 1 (83 f8 01). Mechanism confirmed by experiment: the receiver at IOPCIDeviceDescription.m:70 was an untyped id, and this GCC applies no declared method signature to an id receiver, which is why declaring - (BOOL)isPCIPresent in PCIKernBus.h changed nothing when it was tested (out/i386/mach_kernel, SHA-256 DA6E06AE910CFDC48BA33B8648CBCFB74EE7DCBC904BBA180B9CD86DA06F02AD, where the method was still at 0x20a2f0 and still contained 83 f8 01). The fix is commit 53f1fc3a, which types thePCIBus as PCIKernBus *. In the resulting kernel (out/i386/mach_kernel, SHA-256 A82940452938737FB8514C334434CEAF70B4DC39179A4047B4153D9B589325C1, built 2026-07-26 11:47) the method contains 3c 01 with no 83 f8 01 and has moved to 0x20abc4, the first time it left the 0x20a2f0 it held through six earlier builds, which is what shows the object genuinely recompiled. Held at unexamined deliberately: the entry awaits the measured reference-versus-rebuilt comparison and is not advanced on inspection again, which is what went wrong in the fix pass. Edited directly in ledger.json because the binrecon ledger CLI is forward-only and cannot express the earlier reset (ledger.py:269). See divergences.md Finding 1.
